title: How Does a Helicopter Pilot Eject Without Hitting the Rotor?

analysis.first_line: Eject from a helicopter and you fly straight into the rotor. That's why almost no helicopter has ejection seats.
beats: Hook: The fatal problem with helicopter ejection seats
Introduce the Ka-52 Alligator and its twin rotor setup
Scale comparison: 24-ft rotor blades spinning right over pilots' heads
Step-by-step breakdown: Rotor explosive jettison sequence
Mechanism: Canopy blow-off and rocket extraction seat pull
Problem solved: Two pilots ejected at diverging angles to avoid parachute collision
Real-world proof: The March 2022 combat ejection incident in Ukraine
Looping conclusion: Explaining why pilots never dodge the rotor
analysis.key_number_and_how_it_is_made_feelable: 24 feet rotor blade length, made feelable by visually comparing it side-by-side with a 19-foot pickup truck.
analysis.what_the_viewer_learns: How the Ka-52 attack helicopter allows pilots to safely eject by explosively detaching its rotor blades and pulling pilots upward with rockets at diverging angles.
analysis.ending: smooth loop back to the hook concept ('By the time they rise, it's already gone')
analysis.visual_style: High-fidelity 3D CGI animation with X-ray cutaways perfectly synchronized with every spoken line
analysis.captions: Medium-sized sans-serif font, white text with black outline, centered, animated 1-3 words at a time
analysis.sound: Ambient mechanical whooshes, muffled explosions, rocket firing SFX, subtle suspenseful drone synth music under clear narration
why_it_works: Addresses a common intuitive engineering paradox ('how do you eject without being chopped up?') immediately
Stunning X-ray 3D cutaway animation visualizes exact mechanical sequences step-by-step
Grounds theoretical design in a dramatic real-world historical event (the 2022 combat ejection)
weak_points: At 87 seconds, it pushes past typical short attention spans and could tighten the mid-section
